claims.title: Legendary founding of Gojoseon
claims.summary: According to the Samguk yusa, the mythical Dangun establishes Gojoseon, traditionally regarded as the first Korean kingdom and a shared origin point for both Koreas.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of North Korea: An ancient Korean heritage severed by colonization and Cold War division, forged into a self-isolating state under three generations of a single ruling family.", terralore.co/country/PRK/chronicle#ev-2333bce-legendary-founding-of-gojoseon, claim TL:PRK:event:2333bce:legendary-founding-of-gojoseon, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Silla unifies the peninsula
claims.summary: Allied with Tang China, Silla conquers Baekje in 660 and Goguryeo in 668, then expels the Tang, achieving the first unification of Korea under native rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of North Korea: An ancient Korean heritage severed by colonization and Cold War division, forged into a self-isolating state under three generations of a single ruling family.", terralore.co/country/PRK/chronicle#ev-668-silla-unifies-the-peninsula, claim TL:PRK:event:668:silla-unifies-the-peninsula, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Goryeo dynasty founded
claims.summary: Wang Geon establishes the Goryeo dynasty, which reunifies the peninsula and gives rise to the Western name Korea.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of North Korea: An ancient Korean heritage severed by colonization and Cold War division, forged into a self-isolating state under three generations of a single ruling family.", terralore.co/country/PRK/chronicle#ev-918-goryeo-dynasty-founded, claim TL:PRK:event:918:goryeo-dynasty-founded, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Joseon dynasty founded
claims.summary: Yi Seong-gye founds the long-lived Joseon dynasty, which adopts Neo-Confucianism and under King Sejong creates the hangul alphabet.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of North Korea: An ancient Korean heritage severed by colonization and Cold War division, forged into a self-isolating state under three generations of a single ruling family.", terralore.co/country/PRK/chronicle#ev-1392-joseon-dynasty-founded, claim TL:PRK:event:1392:joseon-dynasty-founded, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Japanese annexation of Korea
claims.summary: Japan formally annexes Korea, ending the Joseon dynasty and beginning thirty-five years of colonial rule over the entire peninsula.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of North Korea: An ancient Korean heritage severed by colonization and Cold War division, forged into a self-isolating state under three generations of a single ruling family.", terralore.co/country/PRK/chronicle#ev-1910-japanese-annexation-of-korea, claim TL:PRK:event:1910:japanese-annexation-of-korea, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Liberation and division at the 38th parallel
claims.summary: Japan's surrender frees Korea but the peninsula is split along the 38th parallel into Soviet and American occupation zones, setting the stage for two rival states.

sources.label: The Korean War and Japan's Recovery
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.title: Founding of the DPRK
claims.summary: The Democratic People's Republic of Korea is proclaimed under Kim Il Sung, weeks after the Republic of Korea is established in the south, institutionalizing the division.

claims.title: North Korea invades the South
claims.summary: North Korean forces cross the 38th parallel, opening the Korean War; the North nearly overruns the peninsula before a US-led UN coalition intervenes.

claims.summary: An armistice halts the fighting and creates the Demilitarized Zone; no peace treaty is signed, freezing the division of the peninsula to the present day.

claims.summary: A new constitution creates the presidency for Kim Il Sung, enshrines Juche as the Workers' Party's guiding idea, and confirms Pyongyang as the capital.

claims.title: Kim Jong Il designated successor
claims.summary: Kim Il Sung formally designates his son Kim Jong Il as his successor, beginning an unprecedented hereditary transfer of power in a communist state.

claims.title: North and South Korea join the UN
claims.summary: Both Korean states are admitted to the United Nations with separate seats, an acknowledgment of the durability of the two-state division.

claims.summary: Kim Il Sung dies after ruling for nearly five decades; he is declared Eternal President and power passes to his son Kim Jong Il.

claims.title: The Arduous March famine
claims.summary: A famine driven by the loss of Soviet support, reduced Chinese aid and flooding kills an estimated several hundred thousand or more North Koreans, a defining national trauma.

claims.summary: North Korea conducts its first underground nuclear test, having withdrawn from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty in 2003 and cycled through failed negotiations.
